To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the forces experienced by subcellular structures of ECs are dependent on the flow profile, and the flow profiles that induce atherosclerosis (low and oscillatory WSS) are predicted to have the most significant impact on mechanotransduction in ECs.

atherogenic flow (reversing and multi-directional) induces different stresses and strains on subcellular components relative to non-therapeutic flow, and the effects of reversing flow are more pronounced than multi-directional flow.

(1) reversing flow (reversing axial WSS) reduces stress on the FA, (2) reversing flow (oscillatory axial WSS) increases stress on ADJ filaments, and (3) multi-directional flow (oscillating axial and transverse WSS) increases shear stress on ADJs in the transverse direction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel computational model that predicts forces on the subcellular components of ECs in atherogenic and non-atherogenic flows.

how flow direction and flow magnitude influence the forces experienced by the subcellular structures in the ECs that are responsible for mechanotransduction, and the subsequent activation of inflammatory signalling pathways.
how the flow direction influences the forces experienced on structural elements in the EC that are believed to be important in mechanotransmission.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
multi-directional flow with reversing axial and lateral components has a greater impact on the mechanical state of ECs than reversing unidirectional flow.
atherosclerosis is a multi-directional phenomenon.
the direction of the flow has a significant effect on the mechanical response of the cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

oscillatory WSS, particularly multi-directional flow, can alter the forces on structural elements in ECs that are known to play roles in mechanotrasnduction, and thus influence the EC inflammatory response.
the flow direction influences the forces experienced at different locations in the cell, and this is likely to affect the signalling pathways activated in the cell.

the multi-scale, multi-physics, multi-component computational model of focally attached endothelial cells is capable of simulating the effects of atherogenically low and oscillating WSS on subcellular structure, and the model predictions are in agreement with the experimental literature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
atherogenic flow patterns can induce distinct responses in ECs, which may be relevant to atherogenesis.
the directionality of flow is an important parameter in the mechanotransduction process.
multi-directional oscillating flow, with reversing transverse and axial flow components, induces a greater degree of strain and stress on EC substructures than unidirectional reversing flow.
